title: Sync SDKs: auth/retry presets, stream ergonomics, and minor version bumps
author: Leila Morgan
release_notes: Backported cohesive auth/retry defaults across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Small ergonomics improvements to streaming APIs (pause/resume, clearer typed errors). Minor SDK version bumps: py 1.9.2, ts 1.27.0, go v1.8.1. No runtime breaking changes expected.
description: Motivation: Multiple product teams reported subtle differences in default auth token refresh timing and retry jitter across SDKs which led to uneven retry storms during rollout tests. This PR unifies a compact credential adapter, aligns retry presets to latency-aware defaults, and polishes streaming ergonomics (pausable iterators / explicit resume API) across Python/TypeScript/Go language bindings. Summary of changes: - Introduce 'cred-compact' adapter used by all SDKs: smaller surface for users who only need default token refresh+prefetch. - Standardize retry presets: default backoff = exponential base 200ms, max backoff 5s, add latency-aware variant that reduces base to 50ms for sub-50ms SLO routes. - Streaming ergonomics: add Iterator.pause()/resume() semantics (py: AsyncIterator.pause_resume; ts: AsyncGeneratorController; go: StreamHandle.Pause/Resume). - Improve typed errors on stream termination (StreamCancelled, AuthRefreshFailed, BackoffExceeded). - Add telemetry tags for credential policy and retry_preset to events emitted by SDKs. - Bump minimum SDK versions and update changelogs across repos. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and reviewed - [x] Cross-language test harness updated - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs snippets and examples updated - [x] Release notes drafted Implementation notes: This PR is a coordination patch in the redwood repository that updates language-agnostic design artifacts plus the CI-driven sync spec used by the three SDK repos. The actual SDK repo patches were generated by the repo tooling and are included as submodule-like artifacts under /sdks/sync-patches/ with per-language diffs applied by the release pipeline. Rationale: keeping the canonical coordination surface in redwood (instead of multiple independent PRs) ensures identical defaults and simplifies rollout testing. Backwards compatibility: pause/resume on streams is additive; the compact credential adapter is opt-in for customers who want lower auth ceremony; retry defaults changed only for the nominal preset; we left legacy presets intact for customers relying on older behavior. See release notes for migration guidance.
